summary.what_it_does: This is a 2012 blog post from Google's Student Blog, not a software tool. It interviews Andrew Widdowson, a Google SRE who joined in 2007, about the role. He explains that SREs are software engineers responsible for keeping Google services reliable and fast, and that the role is distinct from operations. The post describes how SRE teams handle emergency alerts and work on systems like web search. It also gives advice for aspiring SREs, such as learning CS fundamentals, gaining applied Linux experience, and how to apply through the general Software Engineer opening.
notable: First-person interview with a Google SRE about the role
Explains how to indicate SRE interest when applying through the general Software Engineer opening
Advice on preparing: applied Linux, server farms, internships, and public cloud projects
caveats: Dated June 2012; application process and team details may have changed
Reflects one engineer's personal view rather than an official Google description of the role
